questions.learningObjective: evaluate spot and process color in a design critique
questions.stem: On Spot and process color: a designer reviewing a museum exhibition poster notices that a print job needs an exact signature hue that mixing inks cannot match. Which approach addresses this need?

options.text: Use a pre-mixed spot ink specified for that exact color
Add extra process inks beyond the standard four to the press
options.misconception: misunderstands the fixed nature of the four-ink process

options.text: Print the job on a screen instead of on paper stock
options.misconception: changes the medium rather than solving the color matching

options.text: Reduce the entire design to just a single ink color
options.misconception: does not address the need to match one specific hue

questions.explanation: Process color builds hues by overlaying CMYK inks, which cannot reproduce every exact color. A spot color is a pre-mixed ink specified for a precise hue, so using a spot ink is the standard way to match a particular color consistently in print.

The chart simply uses too many colors in total
